The highest and best use analysis is the fulcrum of the appraisal report.The conclusions of thehighest and
of comparable market data that can be used to value the property under appraisal.The highest and best
use of a property provides the framework for the procedures used to estimate market value.
Highest and best use is defined as:
Highest and Best Use
The reasonably probable and legal use of vacant land or an improved property that is physically
possible, appropriately supported, financially feasible, and thatresults in the highest value.The four
criteria the highest and best use must meet are legal permissibility, physical possibility, financial
specific with respect to theuser and timing of the use-thatis adequately supported and results in the
highest present value.Source: Appraisal Institute, The Dictionary of Real Estate Appraisal, 5th ed.
(Chicago: Appraisal Institute,2010).
Market forces create value.It is important to note that the highest and best use of a property is not
determined through subjective analysis by a property owner, adeveloper, ran appraiser The highest and
bestuse of aparticular property is shaped bythe competitive forces of the market inwhich the propertyis
affect that property.The use that maximizes value represents the highest and best use.

Legal Permissibility
This criterion determines which uses are legally permissible. Legal uses are controlled by such things as
private restrictions, zoning ordinances, building codes, and/or environmental regulations. Private
restrictions may prohibit certain uses or specify building requirements such as setbacks, heights, or
cities or counties.Building codes may impose restrictions on construction that result in higher or lower
costs than normal for thearea.Environmental regulations are typically governmental rules pertaining to
cleanair, cleanwater, and/orwetlands.
With regard to legal permissibility, the platte d portion of the subject property is zone dP; Public, butifsold
to a private owner it would be rezoned to Mixed-use or Community Business. These would allow a wide
rangeof commercial and higher-density residential uses.
Physical Possibility
Physical possibility refers to the physical attributes of the property that would affect its suitability for a
particular use.It takes into account such items as size and shape; area; terrain, topography and soils;
accessibility; and/or the risk of natural disasters.Size and shape of the property affects its utility and may
make theproperty particularly suitable or totally unsuitable for a particular use.Analysis of the area
